question: How do MCTS and one-round action enumeration compare under the same allowance of forward simulator transitions per decision on a predeclared set of environment seeds?

prior_study.preservation: Keep all prior files and outcomes unchanged. This is a separate study, not a replacement for the unequal-work comparison.

environment_seed_scope: These values differ from the published prior study's seeds 0 through 4. They have not been evaluated or inspected in this new study before this declaration. No claim is made that they were never used anywhere else.
contextual_control_scope: Random and damage-only greedy perform no sampled forward successor search. Retain their outcomes as context, not as policies that consume the matched transition allowance.

randomness.environment: Each game begins from random.Random(environment_seed). Scenario creation, deck refill and actual environment outcomes use this stream.
randomness.policy: Each game uses a separate random.Random('policy-v1:{base + game_index}') stream.
randomness.search: MCTS starts a fresh search RNG at search_seed for each scenario and retains it across that scenario's five games. No search stream carries across scenarios.
randomness.repeated_conditions: Reuse the five environment starts across the three policy/search bases. These are repeated conditions, not 15 independent environments.
randomness.trajectory_limit: Common initial environment seeds do not produce identical random trajectories when actions consume different draws.

shared_allowance.unit: One completed advance_round call on a cloned state for policy evaluation, including MCTS tree traversal, expansion and rollout. Actual game progression is excluded.
shared_allowance.rationale: 300 is a transparent bounded engineering choice declared before outcomes. It is not selected by a search over these new environments.
shared_allowance.execution_order: Three sequential runs in seed-base order 7,42,99. Each run uses scenario order duel,gauntlet,boss and existing policy order random,greedy,one_round,mcts.
shared_allowance.timing_semantics: Check the safety clock only between complete MCTS simulations or complete equal-action comparator sweeps. This is not a hard wall-clock deadline. Preserve any time-cap result and its measured work.

one_round.candidate_order: Stable original hand index followed by target index, with pass first.
one_round.sweep: Evaluate every legal candidate once using the same starting sample seed for that sweep. Action-dependent draw paths may differ.
one_round.completed_sweeps_target: floor(300 / legal_action_count), unless the safety time cap is reached first.
one_round.requested_samples_per_action: Derived only from the allowance and legal action count. Do not retain the previous independent eight-sample cap.
one_round.evaluation: Terminal result, otherwise the existing unchanged state heuristic.
one_round.insufficient_allowance: If the allowance cannot fund one complete sweep, fail visibly before sampling. Do not return an unevaluated pass or favor a prefix of actions.
one_round.unused_allowance: A remainder smaller than legal_action_count is expected when only complete sweeps are admitted.

mcts.simulation_cap_rationale: A complete nonterminal simulation uses at least one transition. This cap cannot end the study's search earlier than the 300-transition allowance.
mcts.admission: Start a simulation only when remaining allowance is at least the five-round horizon. Complete it, count its actual transitions, then consider another. Do not truncate a simulation to consume the final remainder.
mcts.unused_allowance: A remainder smaller than the horizon is expected conservative admission, not a safety-time shortfall.
mcts.policy_constants: Keep existing exploration, rollout, terminal shaping, heuristic and ranking choices unchanged.
mcts.no_sample: A nonterminal decision with no completed simulation is a visible failure, not an automatic pass.

primary_metric: Clean wins out of five, for each scenario and seed base.
secondary_metrics: Mean shaped game score, explicitly not a win probability.
Average game rounds conditional on a clean win.
Every per-game terminal result, including losses and unfinished 30-round games.
work_metrics: Per-decision requested, used and unused transition allowance.
Actual completed MCTS simulations and actual transitions.
Actual legal candidate count, completed one-round sweeps and transitions.
Exact stop reason and any safety-cap or no-sample event.
Per-game decision counts and their reconciliation to game rounds.
Totals and min/max work by policy, scenario and seed base, retaining unused work.
Environment, Python version, source revision, normalized source hashes and elapsed run time as context.
acceptance: Every used transition count is an integer between zero and 300, and unused equals 300 minus used.
Every comparison decision completes at least one MCTS simulation or one full equal-action sweep.
Comparator used transitions equal legal_action_count times completed_sweeps. No partial or discarded candidate sweep.
MCTS transition counts cover traversal, expansion and rollout exactly once.
Complete simulations and sweeps preserve caller state and legal action identity.
Stop reasons distinguish ordinary allowance remainders, safety-time shortfalls, terminal roots and failures.
Per-game outcomes reconcile with aggregates and decision records. Do not call an unfinished game a loss.
No result-based parameter or seed changes.
failure_policy: Retain all complete, unfavorable, partial and failed runs with their exact settings, exit state, logs and source identity.
A safety cap does not become a completed allowance-budget claim. Keep its outcome visible and identify incomplete work.
Do not silently omit or replace an errored cell. Correct an implementation failure only with a new recorded revision and retained first attempt.
If semantic ambiguity or a necessary design change appears before outcomes, append a dated amendment or new protocol version. Preserve this file.
Do not start the outcome run until interface mapping, implementation source identity and synthetic budget acceptance are recorded.
reporting_limits: Same transition allowance is not equal CPU time, memory, state-cloning cost or action-evaluation overhead.
Policies can consume different actual transition totals because work units must complete and games can end at different rounds.
Five environments per scenario reused across three seed bases are not independent 15-game samples.
No z test, p value, confidence interval or pooled-independent-sample claim.
The policies share the simulator and heuristic. Neither is independent ground truth.
Retain every condition and every losing result. Do not infer general superiority from this small fixed study.
Do not treat old and new environment outcomes as a controlled before/after algorithm effect.

interface.decision_records: Each simulated policy retains transition_work.decision_records in serial game and decision order.
interface.game_mapping: The assembled study adds transition_work.game_decision_ranges with environment_seed, policy_seed, start_index and exclusive stop_index derived cumulatively from game_results rounds. This indexes recorded decisions rather than independently observing them.
interface.incomplete_decisions: Zero-based indices of decisions stopped by time_limit or without transition_allowance. Ordinary exhaustion is checked before the safety clock.
interface.source_identity: Record the tested committed source revision, this committed protocol hash and normalized source hashes before running outcomes. Retain those identities in the combined study.
interface.hash_method: UTF-8 text with LF newlines and no BOM
